recipes.name: Apple Cinnamon Baked Oatmeal
recipes.summary: A pan of soft, cinnamon-spiced oats with apples, walnuts and raisins. Bake once and reheat all week.
steps: Heat the oven to 350°F. Grease a 9x13-inch baking dish.
In a large bowl, mix the oats, flaxseed, brown sugar, baking powder, cinnamon and salt.
In another bowl, whisk the milk, eggs, melted butter and vanilla.
Spread the apples, walnuts and raisins in the dish. Scatter the oat mixture over them, then pour the milk mixture evenly over the top. Press gently so the oats are wet.
Bake 38 to 42 minutes, until golden and set in the center (160°F on a thermometer). Cool 10 minutes before cutting.
recipes.make_ahead: Bake up to 4 days ahead, cool, cover and refrigerate. Reheat squares in the microwave about 1 minute.

freezer.text: Freeze cooled squares wrapped individually for up to 3 months. Microwave from frozen 1 1/2 to 2 minutes.

recipes.kids: Kids can measure the oats and scatter the fruit. For children under 4, chop the walnuts fine.

swaps.dairy_free: Use a plant milk and oil instead of butter.
swaps.nut_free: Use sunflower seeds instead of walnuts.

prep_day.ahead: Bake the whole pan and cut into squares.

recipes.name: Apple Pear Crisp
recipes.summary: Tender apples and pears under a buttery oat and pecan topping. Good warm with a scoop of ice cream.

ingredients.prep: ripe but firm, cored and sliced

steps: Heat the oven to 375°F.
Toss the apples and pears with the lemon juice, sugar, 1 tablespoon flour and cinnamon. Spread in the baking dish.
In a bowl, mix the oats, 1/2 cup flour, brown sugar, pecans and salt. Cut in the cold butter until the mixture forms small clumps.
Sprinkle the topping over the fruit. Bake 40 to 45 minutes, until the topping is golden and the fruit bubbles at the edges.
Cool at least 10 minutes so the juices thicken.
recipes.make_ahead: Make the topping up to 3 days ahead and keep it in the fridge. The baked crisp keeps 4 days in the fridge.

freezer.text: Freeze the baked, cooled crisp for up to 3 months. Thaw in the fridge and warm in a 350°F oven.

recipes.kids: Kids can toss the fruit and rub the butter into the topping with their fingers.

swaps.gluten_free: Use oats labeled gluten-free and a gluten-free flour blend.
swaps.dairy_free: Use coconut oil instead of butter and skip the ice cream.
swaps.nut_free: Leave out the pecans and add 1/4 cup more oats.

prep_day.ahead: Make the topping; slice the fruit the day of.

recipes.name: Waldorf Salad
recipes.summary: Crisp apples, grapes, celery and toasted walnuts in a light, creamy dressing.
steps: Toast the walnuts in a dry skillet over medium heat, stirring, 3 to 5 minutes until fragrant. Let them cool.
Toss the apples with the lemon juice so they stay white.
Stir together the mayonnaise, yogurt, honey and salt.
Add the grapes, celery, walnuts and dressing to the apples and fold together. Serve cold.
recipes.make_ahead: Keeps 1 day in the fridge; the walnuts soften a little.

freezer.text: Do not freeze.

recipes.kids: Cut grapes into quarters for children under 4, and chop the walnuts fine. Honey is not safe for babies under 1 year old.

swaps.dairy_free: Use all mayonnaise.
swaps.egg_free: Use all yogurt instead of mayonnaise.
swaps.nut_free: Use sunflower seeds instead of walnuts.

prep_day.ahead: Chop the celery; toast the walnuts.

recipes.name: Harvest Apple Salad
recipes.summary: Greens with crisp apple, dried cranberries, toasted pecans and pumpkin seeds in a cider vinaigrette.
steps: Toast the pecans and pumpkin seeds in a dry skillet over medium heat, stirring, 3 to 4 minutes, until the seeds start to pop. Cool.
Shake the vinaigrette ingredients in a jar until creamy.
Rinse the apple, then slice it just before serving so it stays crisp.
Toss the greens with most of the vinaigrette. Top with the apple, cranberries, nuts, seeds and feta if using, and drizzle with the rest.
recipes.make_ahead: Toast the nuts and make the vinaigrette up to 5 days ahead.

freezer.text: Do not freeze.

recipes.kids: Kids can shake the dressing jar. Chop the nuts small for children under 4.

swaps.nut_free: Leave out the pecans and double the pumpkin seeds.
swaps.dairy_free: Skip the feta.

prep_day.ahead: Toast nuts and seeds; mix the vinaigrette.

recipes.name: Apple Nachos
recipes.summary: Apple slices on a plate, drizzled with sunflower seed butter and topped with raisins and granola. A nut-free snack kids can build.
steps: Toss the apple slices with the lemon juice and spread them on a large plate, overlapping a little.
Warm the sunflower seed butter in the microwave 10 to 15 seconds so it drizzles, then drizzle it over the apples with a spoon.
Scatter the raisins, granola and chocolate chips (if using) on top. Dust with cinnamon and serve right away.
recipes.make_ahead: Slice the apples just before serving; lemon juice slows browning for a few hours.

freezer.text: Do not freeze.

recipes.kids: Kids can build their own plate. For children under 4, cut apples into thin matchsticks and skip whole raisins.

swaps.nut_free: Sunflower seed butter is nut-free; check that the granola is too.
swaps.dairy_free: Skip the chocolate chips or use dairy-free ones.

recipes.name: Cranberry Orange Muffins
recipes.summary: Tart cranberries and fresh orange in a tender muffin. Freezes well for busy mornings.
steps: Heat the oven to 375°F and line the muffin tin.
Whisk the flour, sugar, baking powder, baking soda and salt in a large bowl.
Zest the orange into a second bowl, then squeeze in the juice (about 1/3 cup). Whisk in the milk, egg, melted butter and vanilla.
Stir the wet mixture into the dry just until no flour shows. Fold in the cranberries.
Fill the cups about three-quarters full. Bake 18 to 22 minutes, until a toothpick in the center comes out clean. Cool 5 minutes in the pan, then on a rack.
recipes.make_ahead: Keep at room temperature up to 2 days.

freezer.text: Freeze cooled muffins in a bag for up to 3 months. Thaw on the counter or warm 20 seconds in the microwave.

recipes.kids: Kids can rinse the cranberries and fill the liners.

swaps.dairy_free: Use a plant milk and oil instead of butter.

prep_day.ahead: Bake a batch; freeze half.

recipes.name: Homemade Cranberry Sauce
recipes.summary: Fresh cranberries simmered with orange and sugar until they burst. Ready in 15 minutes.
steps: Put the sugar, orange juice, water and salt in the saucepan and bring to a boil over medium-high heat, stirring until the sugar dissolves.
Add the cranberries. Simmer, stirring now and then, 8 to 10 minutes, until most of the berries burst.
Stir in the orange zest and cinnamon. The sauce looks loose but thickens as it cools.
Cool to room temperature, about 1 hour, then serve or refrigerate.
recipes.make_ahead: Make up to 1 week ahead and keep covered in the fridge.

freezer.text: Freeze for up to 2 months. Thaw in the fridge overnight.

leftovers.text: Spread on a turkey sandwich, or swirl into yogurt or oatmeal.

recipes.kids: Kids can listen for the berries popping, from a safe distance.

prep_day.ahead: Make the sauce.

recipes.name: Orange Sesame Chicken
recipes.summary: Crisp-edged chicken bites tossed in a fresh orange, ginger and sesame sauce. A takeout favorite made at home.
steps: Start the rice. Whisk the orange zest and juice, soy sauce, honey, vinegar, ginger, garlic and 2 teaspoons cornstarch in a small bowl.
Toss the chicken with 3 tablespoons cornstarch and the salt.

Heat the oil in the skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the chicken in a single layer, turning, 7 to 9 minutes, until browned and a thermometer reads 165°F. Wash your hands after handling raw chicken.
Stir the sauce and pour it into the pan. Simmer 1 to 2 minutes, stirring, until thick and glossy.
Stir in the sesame seeds. Serve over rice with green onions.
recipes.make_ahead: Mix the sauce up to 2 days ahead and refrigerate.

freezer.text: Freeze cooked chicken in sauce for up to 3 months. Thaw in the fridge and reheat to 165°F.

leftovers.text: Pack with rice for lunch; reheat to 165°F.

recipes.kids: Chicken thighs stay tender for kids. Leave the green onions on the side. Honey is not safe for babies under 1 year old.

swaps.gluten_free: Use tamari or a gluten-free soy sauce.

prep_day.ahead: Cut the chicken; mix the sauce.

recipes.name: Winter Citrus Salad
recipes.summary: Grapefruit, oranges and kiwi with pomegranate seeds, honey and mint. Bright fruit for the darkest months.
steps: Rinse the fruit. Slice the top and bottom off each grapefruit and orange, then cut away the peel and white pith, following the curve of the fruit.
Slice the grapefruit and oranges into rounds, or cut between the membranes to free the segments. Save the juice.
Arrange the citrus and kiwi on a platter. Scatter the pomegranate seeds over the top.
Stir the honey into 2 tablespoons of the saved juice and drizzle over. Finish with the mint.
recipes.make_ahead: Cut the citrus up to 1 day ahead; add the kiwi and mint just before serving.

freezer.text: Do not freeze.

recipes.kids: Grown-ups do the peeling with the knife; kids can arrange the fruit and pick pomegranate seeds. Honey is not safe for babies under 1 year old.

swaps.vegan: Use maple syrup instead of honey.

prep_day.ahead: Peel and slice the citrus.

recipes.name: Broiled Brown Sugar Grapefruit
recipes.summary: Grapefruit halves with a bubbly, caramelized brown sugar top. A warm breakfast treat in 10 minutes.
steps: Set an oven rack about 4 inches from the broiler and heat the broiler.
Rinse the grapefruit before cutting. Run a paring knife around each segment so it lifts out easily later.
Set the halves cut side up on the baking sheet. Brush with butter if using. Mix the brown sugar and cinnamon and sprinkle over the tops.
Broil 4 to 6 minutes, watching closely, until the sugar bubbles and browns. Cool 2 minutes and serve with a spoon.
recipes.make_ahead: Section the halves up to 1 day ahead; cover and refrigerate.

freezer.text: Do not freeze.

recipes.kids: Kids can sprinkle the sugar. Grapefruit can interact with some medicines, so check labels if anyone in the family takes them.

swaps.dairy_free: Skip the butter.

prep_day.ahead: Halve and section the grapefruit.

recipes.name: Grapefruit Avocado Salad
recipes.summary: Juicy grapefruit and creamy avocado over peppery greens with a honey-citrus dressing.
steps: Rinse the grapefruit. Cut away the peel and pith, then cut out the segments over a bowl to catch the juice.
Whisk 2 tablespoons of the grapefruit juice with the olive oil, honey, salt and pepper.
Spread the arugula on a platter. Top with the grapefruit, avocado and onion.
Drizzle with the dressing and serve right away.
recipes.make_ahead: Cut the grapefruit up to 1 day ahead. Slice the avocado just before serving.

freezer.text: Do not freeze.

recipes.kids: Honey is not safe for babies under 1 year old.

swaps.vegan: Use maple syrup instead of honey.

prep_day.ahead: Section the grapefruit; mix the dressing.

recipes.name: Salmon with Grapefruit Avocado Salsa
recipes.summary: Roasted salmon topped with a fresh salsa of grapefruit, avocado, lime and cilantro.
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F and line the baking sheet with parchment.
Set the salmon skin side down on the sheet. Rub with the oil and sprinkle with salt, pepper and chili powder.
Roast 12 to 14 minutes, until the fish flakes easily and a thermometer in the thickest part reads 145°F.
While it roasts, gently stir together the grapefruit, avocado, onion, jalapeño (if using), cilantro, lime juice and salt.
Spoon the salsa over the salmon to serve.
recipes.make_ahead: Chop the onion and section the grapefruit up to 1 day ahead. Add the avocado just before serving.

freezer.text: Freeze raw salmon instead, 2 to 3 months for best quality.

leftovers.text: Flake cold leftover salmon over greens for lunch, or reheat to 165°F.

recipes.kids: Check for bones by running a finger along the fillet before serving young children.

prep_day.ahead: Section the grapefruit; chop the onion and cilantro.

recipes.name: Grapefruit Granita
recipes.summary: Fresh grapefruit juice frozen and scraped into icy, sweet-tart flakes. Only three ingredients.
steps: Rinse the grapefruit, then cut in half and squeeze out the juice. Strain out the seeds.
Warm the water and sugar in a small pan or the microwave, stirring, just until the sugar dissolves. Stir it into the juice.
Pour into the pan and freeze 45 minutes, until ice forms at the edges. Scrape and stir with a fork.
Freeze, scraping every 30 to 45 minutes, until it is all fluffy ice crystals, about 3 hours in all.
Scrape once more and spoon into chilled glasses. Top with mint if you like.
recipes.make_ahead: Keeps 1 week in the freezer, covered. Scrape again with a fork before serving.

freezer.text: Keep covered in the freezer up to 1 week.

recipes.kids: Kids can scrape the ice with a fork. Grapefruit can interact with some medicines, so check labels if anyone in the family takes them.

prep_day.ahead: Juice the grapefruit and start the freezing.

recipes.name: Tropical Smoothie
recipes.summary: Pineapple, mango and banana blended with yogurt and orange juice. Tastes like vacation.
steps: Put the orange juice and yogurt in the blender first, then the banana, pineapple and mango.
Blend on high until smooth, about 1 minute. Add a splash more juice if it is too thick to pour.
recipes.make_ahead: Pack the fruit into freezer bags as ready-to-blend kits.

freezer.text: Freeze kits of the cut fruit for up to 3 months; blend straight from frozen.

recipes.kids: Kids can drop the fruit in and press the button with a grown-up.

swaps.dairy_free: Use a dairy-free yogurt or more juice.

prep_day.ahead: Bag smoothie kits for the freezer.

recipes.name: Fresh Mango Salsa
recipes.summary: Sweet mango with red pepper, onion, cilantro and lime. Scoop with chips or spoon over tacos, chicken or fish.
steps: Rinse the mangoes, pepper and cilantro. Wear gloves or wash your hands well after seeding the jalapeño.
Combine the mango, bell pepper, onion, jalapeño and cilantro in a bowl.
Stir in the lime juice and salt. Let it sit 10 minutes for the flavors to mix, then taste and add more salt or lime if needed.
recipes.make_ahead: Keeps 2 days in the fridge, covered.

freezer.text: Do not freeze; the mango turns mushy.

recipes.kids: For a mild salsa, leave out the jalapeño and let grown-ups add hot sauce.

prep_day.ahead: Make the salsa.

recipes.name: Mango Coconut Chia Pudding
recipes.summary: Chia seeds soaked overnight in coconut milk, layered with fresh mango. Make jars for the week.
steps: Whisk the coconut milk, milk, chia seeds, maple syrup and vanilla in a bowl.
Let stand 10 minutes, then whisk again to break up clumps.
Divide among the jars, cover and refrigerate at least 4 hours or overnight, until thick.
Toss the mango with the lime juice and spoon on top before serving. Sprinkle with coconut if using.
recipes.make_ahead: Keeps 4 days in the fridge. Add the mango the day you eat it, or up to 1 day ahead.

freezer.text: The texture suffers when frozen.

recipes.kids: Kids can stir and spoon the pudding into jars.

swaps.dairy_free: Use more coconut milk or another plant milk instead of the milk.

prep_day.ahead: Fill jars for 4 days.

recipes.name: Peach Mango Smoothie
recipes.summary: Peaches and mango blended thick with yogurt and a little honey. Use fresh, frozen or canned peaches.

ingredients.prep: pitted and sliced, or 1 1/2 cups frozen

steps: Rinse fresh peaches before slicing.
Put the milk and yogurt in the blender, then the peaches, mango, honey and vanilla.
Blend until smooth, about 1 minute. Add a few ice cubes if you used fresh peaches and want it colder.
recipes.make_ahead: Bag the peaches and mango together for the freezer.

freezer.text: Freeze fruit kits up to 3 months; blend from frozen.

recipes.kids: Honey is not safe for babies under 1 year old.

swaps.dairy_free: Use a plant milk and dairy-free yogurt.

prep_day.ahead: Bag smoothie kits for the freezer.

recipes.name: Mango Lime Chicken Rice Bowls
recipes.summary: Chili-lime chicken over rice with black beans, fresh mango and a squeeze of lime.
steps: Cook the rice according to the package directions.
Toss the chicken with the lime zest and juice, oil, chili powder, cumin, garlic powder and salt.
Cook the chicken in a skillet over medium-high heat, 5 to 6 minutes per side, until a thermometer reads 165°F. Rest 5 minutes, then slice. Wash your hands and anything that touched the raw chicken.
Warm the beans in a small pan or the microwave. Mix the mango, onion and cilantro.
Fill bowls with rice, beans, chicken and the mango mixture. Serve with lime wedges and avocado if you like.
recipes.make_ahead: Cook the rice and chicken up to 3 days ahead. Keep the mango mixture separate.

freezer.text: Freeze cooked chicken and rice (without mango) for up to 3 months. Reheat to 165°F.

leftovers.text: Pack a bowl for lunch; reheat the chicken and rice to 165°F and add the mango cold.

recipes.kids: Serve the parts separately for picky eaters.

swaps.meatless: Use a second can of black beans instead of chicken.

prep_day.ahead: Cook the rice and chicken; dice the mango.

recipes.name: Tropical Fruit Salad
recipes.summary: Pineapple, mango and kiwi tossed with lime juice, honey and fresh mint.
steps: Rinse the fruit before peeling and cutting.
Combine the pineapple, mango and kiwi in a large bowl.
Stir the lime juice and honey together, pour over and toss gently. Add the banana and mint just before serving.
recipes.make_ahead: Keeps 2 days in the fridge without the banana.

freezer.text: Do not freeze; blend leftovers into smoothies.

recipes.kids: Kids can slice kiwi and banana with a butter knife. Honey is not safe for babies under 1 year old.

swaps.vegan: Use maple syrup instead of honey.

prep_day.ahead: Cut the pineapple and mango.

recipes.name: Sheet-Pan Pineapple Pork Tacos
recipes.summary: Chili-rubbed pork and pineapple roasted on one pan, tucked into warm tortillas with onion, cilantro and lime. Inspired by tacos al pastor.

ingredients.prep: boneless, sliced 1/4 inch thick and cut in strips

steps: Heat the oven to 450°F. Mix the chili powder, paprika, cumin, oregano, garlic, salt, vinegar and oil in a bowl. Add the pork and toss to coat. Wash your hands after handling raw pork.
Spread the pork on one side of the baking sheet and the pineapple on the other, each in a single layer.
Roast 20 to 25 minutes, stirring once, until the pork is browned at the edges and a thermometer reads at least 145°F. Rest 3 minutes, then chop the pork and pineapple together.
Fill the warm tortillas with the pork and pineapple. Top with onion and cilantro, and squeeze lime over each taco.

safety.food: beef, pork or lamb steaks, chops and roasts

recipes.make_ahead: Marinate the pork in the spice mix up to 1 day ahead in the fridge.

freezer.text: Freeze the cooked pork and pineapple for up to 3 months. Reheat to 165°F.

leftovers.text: Spoon over rice or into a quesadilla; reheat to 165°F.

recipes.kids: Kids can squeeze the lime and choose toppings. The spice rub is flavorful, not hot.

swaps.gluten_free: Corn tortillas are usually gluten-free; check the package.
swaps.meatless: Use 2 cans drained black beans, warmed with the spices, instead of pork.

prep_day.ahead: Slice and marinate the pork; cut the pineapple.

recipes.name: Pineapple Cashew Fried Rice
recipes.summary: Day-old rice stir-fried with pineapple, eggs, peas and carrots, and finished with toasted cashews.

ingredients.prep: cooked a day ahead and chilled (makes about 4 cups)

steps: Heat 1 teaspoon oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Scramble the eggs until no liquid egg remains (egg dishes are done at 160°F). Move to a plate.
Add the rest of the oil and raise the heat to medium-high. Cook the onion 3 minutes, then the garlic 30 seconds.
Add the peas and carrots and cook 2 minutes. Add the rice, breaking up clumps, and cook, stirring now and then, until hot, about 5 minutes.
Push the rice aside, add the pineapple and let it brown 2 minutes. Stir in the soy sauce, sesame oil, eggs, cashews and green onions.
recipes.make_ahead: Cook and chill the rice up to 3 days ahead; cold rice fries best.

freezer.text: Freeze for up to 2 months. Reheat in a skillet to 165°F.

leftovers.text: Reheat to 165°F and pack for lunch.

recipes.kids: Chop the cashews fine for children under 4.

swaps.gluten_free: Use tamari or a gluten-free soy sauce.
swaps.nut_free: Leave out the cashews; add diced cooked chicken or ham.

prep_day.ahead: Cook and chill the rice.

recipes.name: Carrot Raisin Salad
recipes.summary: Shredded carrots, plump raisins and crushed pineapple in a light, tangy dressing. A potluck classic.
steps: Shred the carrots and put them in a bowl with the raisins and pineapple.
Stir together the mayonnaise, yogurt, lemon juice, sugar and salt.
Fold the dressing into the carrots. Chill at least 30 minutes, or serve right away.
recipes.make_ahead: Keeps 3 days in the fridge.

freezer.text: Do not freeze.

recipes.kids: Kids can stir in the raisins and pineapple. For children under 4, chop the raisins.

swaps.dairy_free: Use all mayonnaise.

prep_day.ahead: Make the salad.

recipes.name: Watermelon Cucumber Feta Salad
recipes.summary: Cold watermelon and cucumber with salty feta, mint and lime. A cool side for hot days.
steps: Rinse the outside of the watermelon and cucumber before cutting.
Put the watermelon, cucumber and onion in a large bowl.
Drizzle with the lime juice and oil, add a pinch of salt and toss gently.
Top with the feta and mint and serve cold.
recipes.make_ahead: Cut the melon up to 1 day ahead. Toss with the dressing and feta just before serving.

freezer.text: Do not freeze.

recipes.kids: Kids can tear the mint and sprinkle the feta.

swaps.dairy_free: Leave out the feta.

prep_day.ahead: Cube the watermelon.

recipes.name: Watermelon Agua Fresca
recipes.summary: Fresh watermelon blended with water and lime, then strained. A light Mexican-style fruit drink.
steps: Rinse the watermelon before cutting.
Blend the watermelon and water until smooth, in two batches if needed.
Pour through a strainer into a pitcher, pressing on the pulp. Stir in the lime juice. Taste and stir in sugar if the melon is not very sweet.
Serve over ice with mint if you like.
recipes.make_ahead: Keeps 2 days in the fridge; stir before pouring.

freezer.text: Freeze in ice-pop molds or ice cube trays.

recipes.kids: Kids can squeeze the limes and stir.

prep_day.ahead: Blend and chill.

recipes.name: Watermelon Fruit Pizza
recipes.summary: Thick rounds of watermelon spread with honey yogurt and topped with berries and kiwi, cut into wedges.

ingredients.prep: 2 round slices, 1 inch thick, from the middle of the melon

steps: Rinse the watermelon and fruit. A grown-up cuts the round slices and trims off the rind.
Stir the honey into the yogurt and spread it over each round, leaving a little edge.
Top with strawberries, blueberries and kiwi.
Cut each round into 6 wedges and serve right away.
recipes.make_ahead: Cut the fruit up to 1 day ahead. Build the pizzas just before serving.

freezer.text: Do not freeze.

recipes.kids: Kids love decorating their own round. Cut blueberries in half for children under 4. Honey is not safe for babies under 1 year old.

swaps.dairy_free: Use a dairy-free yogurt.

prep_day.ahead: Wash and slice the berries and kiwi.

recipes.name: Summer Melon Salad
recipes.summary: Watermelon, cantaloupe and honeydew with a honey-lime dressing and mint.
steps: Scrub the outside of each melon under running water before cutting; a knife can carry germs from the rind into the fruit.
Cut or scoop the melons and combine in a large bowl.
Stir the lime juice and honey together, pour over and toss. Scatter the mint over the top.
recipes.make_ahead: Cut melon keeps 3 days in the fridge.

freezer.text: Do not freeze; blend leftovers into agua fresca or smoothies.

recipes.kids: Kids can use the melon baller with help. Honey is not safe for babies under 1 year old.

swaps.vegan: Use maple syrup instead of honey.

prep_day.ahead: Cut the melons.

recipes.name: Watermelon Lime Ice Pops
recipes.summary: Blended watermelon and lime frozen into pops. Only three ingredients and no added dye.
steps: Rinse the watermelon before cutting.
Blend the watermelon, lime juice and honey until smooth.
Pour into the molds, add the sticks and freeze at least 6 hours, until solid.
Run the molds under warm water for a few seconds to loosen the pops.
recipes.make_ahead: Keeps 1 month in the freezer.

freezer.text: Keep frozen up to 1 month.

recipes.kids: Kids can pour the mix into the molds. Honey is not safe for babies under 1 year old.

prep_day.ahead: Blend and freeze the pops.

recipes.name: Cantaloupe Cottage Cheese Bowls
recipes.summary: A diner classic: wedges of cantaloupe filled with cottage cheese, blueberries and a little granola.
steps: Scrub the cantaloupe under running water and dry it before cutting.
Cut the melon into quarters and scoop out the seeds.
Fill each quarter with 1/2 cup cottage cheese. Top with blueberries and granola, and drizzle with honey if you like.
recipes.make_ahead: Cut melon keeps 3 days in the fridge, covered.

freezer.text: Do not freeze.

recipes.kids: Cut the melon off the rind and into small pieces for young children. Cut blueberries in half for children under 4.

prep_day.ahead: Cut and seed the cantaloupe.

recipes.name: Honeydew Mint Smoothie
recipes.summary: Cool, pale green smoothie of honeydew, banana, yogurt, lime and fresh mint.
steps: Scrub the honeydew under running water before cutting.
Blend everything until smooth, about 1 minute. Add a few ice cubes for a colder, thicker drink.
recipes.make_ahead: Freeze cubed melon and banana ahead so the smoothie is frosty.

freezer.text: Freeze the cut fruit for up to 3 months.

recipes.kids: Kids can count the mint leaves into the blender.

swaps.dairy_free: Use a dairy-free yogurt.

prep_day.ahead: Cube and freeze the melon.

recipes.name: Fruit Kabobs with Yogurt Dip
recipes.summary: Melon, pineapple, strawberries and grapes on skewers with a honey-vanilla yogurt dip. Party food that disappears.
steps: Scrub the melons and pineapple under running water before cutting. Rinse the berries and grapes.
Thread the fruit onto the skewers in a pattern, about 6 or 7 pieces each.
Stir the yogurt, honey, vanilla and cinnamon together for the dip. Serve the kabobs cold with the dip.
recipes.make_ahead: Make kabobs up to 1 day ahead; cover and refrigerate.

freezer.text: Do not freeze.

recipes.kids: Kids can thread the fruit. For children under 4, skip the skewers, cut grapes in quarters and serve the fruit in a bowl. Honey is not safe for babies under 1 year old.

swaps.dairy_free: Use a dairy-free yogurt.

prep_day.ahead: Cut the fruit and build the kabobs.

recipes.name: Cantaloupe Mozzarella Salad
recipes.summary: Sweet cantaloupe with fresh mozzarella, arugula and basil, finished with olive oil and a little balsamic.
steps: Scrub the cantaloupe under running water before cutting.
Spread the arugula on a platter. Top with the cantaloupe and mozzarella.
Drizzle with the oil and vinegar, sprinkle with salt and pepper, and scatter the basil over the top.
recipes.make_ahead: Cut the melon up to 1 day ahead. Assemble just before serving.

freezer.text: Do not freeze.

recipes.kids: Kids can tear the basil and mozzarella.

swaps.dairy_free: Use diced avocado instead of mozzarella.

prep_day.ahead: Cut the cantaloupe.

recipes.name: Sausage with Roasted Grapes and Onions
recipes.summary: Italian sausages roasted on one pan with red grapes and onion until the grapes turn jammy. An Italian farmhouse dish.
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F.
Toss the grapes and onion with the oil, salt and pepper on the baking sheet. Nestle in the sausages and rosemary sprigs.
Roast 25 to 30 minutes, turning the sausages once, until they are browned, a thermometer in the center reads 160°F, and the grapes are soft and starting to burst.
Drizzle the balsamic over the grapes and onions, stir, and serve.
recipes.make_ahead: Cut the onion and wash the grapes up to 2 days ahead.

freezer.text: Freeze cooked sausages and grapes for up to 2 months. Reheat to 165°F.

leftovers.text: Slice the sausage into a sandwich roll with the grapes and onions; reheat to 165°F.

recipes.kids: Slice the sausage into half-moons and cut the grapes for children under 4. Cut grapes lengthwise into quarters for children under 4; whole grapes are a choking risk.

swaps.meatless: Use plant-based sausages and cook by the package directions.

prep_day.ahead: Wash the grapes; cut the onion.

recipes.name: Broccoli Grape Salad
recipes.summary: Crunchy raw broccoli with grapes, sunflower seeds and dried cranberries in a sweet-tangy dressing. A cookout favorite.
steps: Rinse the broccoli and grapes and pat dry.
Whisk the mayonnaise, yogurt, vinegar, sugar and salt.
Toss the broccoli, grapes, onion and cranberries with the dressing.
Chill at least 30 minutes. Stir in the sunflower seeds just before serving so they stay crunchy.
recipes.make_ahead: Keeps 3 days in the fridge; add the seeds the day you serve it.

freezer.text: Do not freeze.

recipes.kids: Cut grapes lengthwise into quarters for children under 4; whole grapes are a choking risk.

swaps.dairy_free: Use all mayonnaise.

prep_day.ahead: Make the salad; keep the seeds separate.

recipes.name: Green Kiwi Smoothie
recipes.summary: Spinach, kiwi, banana and pineapple blended with milk and chia. Sweet enough that kids ask for it.
steps: Pour the milk into the blender and add the spinach. Blend until no leaf bits remain.
Add the kiwi, banana, pineapple and chia seeds and blend until smooth, about 1 minute. Serve right away.
recipes.make_ahead: Freeze bags of the fruit and spinach for quick mornings.

freezer.text: Freeze smoothie kits for up to 3 months.

recipes.kids: Call it a monster smoothie; the green color is the fun part.

swaps.dairy_free: Use a plant milk.

prep_day.ahead: Bag smoothie kits.

recipes.name: Banana Walnut Bread
recipes.summary: A moist loaf with plenty of ripe banana and toasted walnuts. The best use for spotty bananas.
steps: Heat the oven to 350°F. Grease the loaf pan.
Mash the bananas in a large bowl. Whisk in the melted butter, brown sugar, eggs and vanilla.
Add the flour, baking soda, salt and cinnamon and stir just until combined. Fold in the walnuts.
Scrape into the pan. Bake 55 to 65 minutes, until a toothpick in the center comes out with only a few moist crumbs. Cover loosely with foil after 40 minutes if the top browns too fast.
Cool 15 minutes in the pan, then turn out onto a rack.
recipes.make_ahead: Keeps 3 days wrapped at room temperature.

freezer.text: Freeze whole or sliced, wrapped well, for up to 3 months.

recipes.kids: Kids can mash the bananas. Chop the walnuts fine for children under 4.

swaps.dairy_free: Use 1/3 cup vegetable oil instead of butter.
swaps.nut_free: Leave out the walnuts or use chocolate chips.

prep_day.ahead: Bake the loaf; slice and freeze half.

recipes.name: Lemon Blueberry Muffins
recipes.summary: Bursting with blueberries and bright with fresh lemon zest and juice.
steps: Heat the oven to 375°F and line the muffin tin.
Whisk the flour, sugar, baking powder, baking soda and salt in a large bowl.
Zest the lemon into a second bowl, then squeeze in the juice (about 3 tablespoons). Whisk in the yogurt, eggs, melted butter and vanilla.
Stir the wet mixture into the dry just until no flour shows. Gently fold in the blueberries.
Fill the cups about three-quarters full. Bake 20 to 24 minutes, until a toothpick in the center comes out clean. Cool 5 minutes in the pan, then on a rack.
recipes.make_ahead: Keep at room temperature up to 2 days.

freezer.text: Freeze cooled muffins in a bag for up to 3 months.

recipes.kids: Kids can zest the lemon with help and fold in the berries.

swaps.dairy_free: Use a dairy-free yogurt and oil instead of butter.

prep_day.ahead: Bake a batch; freeze half.

recipes.name: Mixed Berry Cobbler
recipes.summary: Blueberries, raspberries and blackberries baked under soft, golden biscuit topping.
steps: Heat the oven to 375°F. Rinse the berries gently and drain well.
Toss the berries with 1/2 cup sugar, cornstarch and lemon juice. Spread in the baking dish.
Mix the flour, 3 tablespoons sugar, baking powder and salt. Cut in the butter until it looks like coarse crumbs. Stir in the milk and vanilla just until a soft dough forms.
Drop spoonfuls of dough over the berries, leaving gaps for steam. Bake 35 to 40 minutes, until the topping is golden and the fruit bubbles in the center.
Cool 15 minutes so the filling thickens.
recipes.make_ahead: Keeps 3 days in the fridge. Warm portions in the microwave.

freezer.text: Freeze the filling raw (berries with sugar and cornstarch) for up to 3 months; bake from frozen with fresh topping, adding about 15 minutes.

recipes.kids: Kids can drop the biscuit dough on top.

swaps.dairy_free: Use a plant milk and cold coconut oil.

prep_day.ahead: Mix the berry filling.

recipes.name: Berry Chia Jam
recipes.summary: A quick fridge jam: raspberries and blackberries simmered soft and thickened with chia seeds. No pectin, much less sugar.
steps: Put the berries in the saucepan over medium heat. Cook, stirring, 5 to 8 minutes, until they break down and bubble.
Mash to the texture you like. Stir in the maple syrup and lemon juice.
Take the pan off the heat and stir in the chia seeds. Let stand 10 minutes, then stir again.
Spoon into the jar. It thickens more as it chills, about 30 minutes.
recipes.make_ahead: Keeps about 1 week in the fridge. This is a fridge jam, not a canned one.

freezer.text: Freeze in small containers for up to 3 months; thaw in the fridge.

recipes.kids: Spread on toast, stir into yogurt or oatmeal, or use in a sandwich.

prep_day.ahead: Make a jar for the week.

recipes.name: Berry Oat Crumble Bars
recipes.summary: A buttery oat crust and crumble with a layer of raspberries and blackberries and a few sliced almonds.
steps: Heat the oven to 350°F. Line the pan with parchment, leaving some hanging over the sides.
Mix the flour, oats, brown sugar, baking powder and salt. Stir in the melted butter until crumbly.
Press two-thirds of the mixture firmly into the pan. Stir the almonds into the rest.
Toss the berries with the sugar, cornstarch and lemon juice, mashing a few. Spread over the crust and sprinkle the almond crumble on top.
Bake 38 to 42 minutes, until golden and bubbling at the edges. Cool completely, about 1 hour, before lifting out and cutting.
recipes.make_ahead: Keeps 4 days in the fridge, covered.

freezer.text: Freeze cut bars in a single layer, then bag, for up to 3 months.

recipes.kids: Kids can press the crust into the pan.

swaps.gluten_free: Use a gluten-free flour blend and oats labeled gluten-free.
swaps.dairy_free: Use melted coconut oil instead of butter.

prep_day.ahead: Bake and cut the bars.

recipes.name: Berry Yogurt Ice Pops
recipes.summary: Creamy yogurt swirled with mashed raspberries and blackberries, frozen on a stick.
steps: Stir the yogurt, 2 tablespoons honey and vanilla together.
Mash the berries with the rest of the honey in another bowl.
Spoon yogurt and berries into the molds in layers, then swirl with a skewer.
Add sticks and freeze at least 6 hours. Run the molds under warm water to release.
recipes.make_ahead: Keeps 1 month in the freezer.

freezer.text: Keep frozen up to 1 month.

recipes.kids: Kids can layer the molds. Honey is not safe for babies under 1 year old.

swaps.dairy_free: Use a thick dairy-free yogurt.

prep_day.ahead: Fill and freeze the pops.

recipes.name: Summer Berry Pecan Salad
recipes.summary: Greens with strawberries, raspberries, blackberries, toasted pecans and goat cheese in a balsamic dressing.
steps: Toast the pecans in a dry skillet over medium heat, stirring, 3 to 5 minutes. Cool and chop.
Rinse the berries gently and pat dry.
Shake the dressing ingredients in a jar.
Toss the greens with most of the dressing. Top with the berries, pecans and goat cheese if using, and drizzle with the rest.
recipes.make_ahead: Toast the pecans and make the dressing up to 5 days ahead.

freezer.text: Do not freeze.

recipes.kids: Chop the pecans small for children under 4. Honey is not safe for babies under 1 year old.

swaps.nut_free: Use sunflower seeds instead of pecans.
swaps.dairy_free: Skip the goat cheese.

prep_day.ahead: Toast the pecans; mix the dressing.

recipes.name: Mixed Berry Flax Smoothie
recipes.summary: Frozen berries, banana and yogurt with ground flaxseed for fiber. Thick, purple and quick.
steps: Pour the milk and yogurt into the blender, then add the banana, berries and flaxseed.
Blend until smooth, about 1 minute. Add a splash more milk if it is too thick.
recipes.make_ahead: Keep ground flaxseed in the fridge or freezer so it stays fresh.

freezer.text: Blend fresh; freeze leftovers as ice pops.

recipes.kids: Kids can measure the berries.

swaps.dairy_free: Use a plant milk and dairy-free yogurt.

recipes.name: Pear Walnut Salad
recipes.summary: Sliced ripe pears, toasted walnuts and a little blue cheese over greens with a maple-dijon vinaigrette.
steps: Toast the walnuts in a dry skillet over medium heat, stirring, 3 to 5 minutes. Cool and chop.
Shake the vinaigrette ingredients in a jar.
Rinse the pears, then slice them just before serving.
Toss the greens and onion with most of the vinaigrette. Top with pears, walnuts and blue cheese if using, and drizzle with the rest.
recipes.make_ahead: Toast the walnuts and mix the dressing up to 5 days ahead.

freezer.text: Do not freeze.

recipes.kids: Chop the walnuts small for children under 4.

swaps.nut_free: Use pumpkin seeds instead of walnuts.
swaps.dairy_free: Skip the blue cheese.

prep_day.ahead: Toast the walnuts; mix the vinaigrette.

recipes.name: Pear and Cheddar Grilled Cheese
recipes.summary: Sharp cheddar and thin slices of sweet pear grilled until golden, with a little honey mustard.
steps: Stir the mustard and honey together and spread thinly on 4 slices of bread.
Sprinkle each with 1/4 cup cheese, then a layer of pear slices and another 1/4 cup cheese. Top with the remaining bread.
Butter the outsides. Cook in a skillet over medium-low heat 3 to 4 minutes per side, pressing gently, until golden and the cheese melts.
Cut in half and serve warm.
recipes.make_ahead: Slice the pears just before cooking.

freezer.text: Best made fresh.

recipes.kids: Skip the mustard for picky eaters; the pear adds sweetness kids like. Honey is not safe for babies under 1 year old.

swaps.dairy_free: Use dairy-free cheese and oil.

recipes.name: Baked Pears with Walnuts and Maple
recipes.summary: Pear halves baked soft with a maple, oat and walnut filling. Serve warm with yogurt.

ingredients.prep: ripe but firm, halved and cored

steps: Heat the oven to 375°F.
Rinse the pears. Halve them, scoop out the cores and set them cut side up in the dish.
Mix the walnuts, oats, 1 tablespoon maple syrup, butter and cinnamon. Spoon into the hollows.
Drizzle the rest of the maple syrup over the pears and pour the water into the dish.
Bake 25 to 30 minutes, until a knife slides easily into the pears. Serve warm with yogurt and the pan juices.
recipes.make_ahead: Keeps 3 days in the fridge; warm in the microwave.

freezer.text: The pears turn mushy when frozen.

recipes.kids: Kids can fill the pear halves. Chop the walnuts fine for children under 4.

swaps.dairy_free: Use coconut oil and a dairy-free yogurt.
swaps.nut_free: Use more oats and sunflower seeds instead of walnuts.

prep_day.ahead: Bake a pan for snacks.

recipes.name: Spiced Pear Oatmeal
recipes.summary: Creamy stovetop oats cooked with diced pear, cinnamon and ginger.
steps: Bring the water, milk and salt to a simmer in the saucepan over medium heat. Watch so it does not boil over.
Stir in the oats, pear, cinnamon and ginger. Cook, stirring often, 5 to 7 minutes, until thick and the pear is tender.
Stir in the maple syrup. Serve topped with pecans if you like.
recipes.make_ahead: Keeps 4 days in the fridge; add a splash of milk when you reheat.

freezer.text: Freeze single portions for up to 2 months.

recipes.kids: Kids can stir in the toppings.

swaps.dairy_free: Use a plant milk.

prep_day.ahead: Cook a pot for the week.

recipes.name: Stone Fruit Crisp
recipes.summary: Peaches, plums and cherries baked under a crunchy oat and almond topping. Summer in a pan.
steps: Heat the oven to 375°F. Rinse the fruit.
Toss the peaches, plums and cherries with the sugar, cornstarch, lemon juice and vanilla. Spread in the baking dish.
Mix the oats, flour, brown sugar, almonds, cinnamon and salt. Work in the butter with your fingers until clumpy.
Scatter the topping over the fruit. Bake 40 to 45 minutes, until golden and bubbling in the center.
Cool at least 10 minutes before serving.
recipes.make_ahead: Keeps 3 days in the fridge.

freezer.text: Freeze the baked crisp for up to 3 months; reheat at 350°F.

recipes.kids: Kids can toss the fruit and crumble the topping. A grown-up pits the fruit.

swaps.gluten_free: Use oats labeled gluten-free and a gluten-free flour blend.
swaps.dairy_free: Use cold coconut oil.

prep_day.ahead: Make the topping; pit the cherries.

recipes.name: Peach Cobbler
recipes.summary: Juicy cinnamon peaches under a tender, golden batter that bakes up around the fruit. A Southern favorite.

ingredients.prep: peeled and sliced (about 6 cups), or 3 cans sliced peaches, drained

steps: Heat the oven to 350°F. Put the butter in the baking dish and set it in the oven to melt.
Simmer the peaches, 1/2 cup sugar, cinnamon and lemon juice in a saucepan over medium heat for 5 minutes.
Whisk the flour, 3/4 cup sugar, baking powder and salt. Whisk in the milk and vanilla until smooth.
Pour the batter over the melted butter. Do not stir. Spoon the peaches and their juice evenly over the batter.
Bake 40 to 45 minutes, until the top is golden and the batter is set. Cool 15 minutes before serving.
recipes.make_ahead: Keeps 3 days in the fridge.

freezer.text: Freeze baked cobbler up to 3 months; reheat at 350°F until warm.

recipes.kids: Kids can whisk the batter. A grown-up handles the hot dish with the melted butter.

swaps.dairy_free: Use a plant milk and dairy-free butter.

prep_day.ahead: Slice the peaches.

recipes.name: Grilled Chicken with Peach Salsa
recipes.summary: Simple grilled chicken topped with a fresh salsa of peaches, red onion, jalapeño, cilantro and lime.
steps: Rinse the peaches, cilantro and jalapeño. Stir the salsa ingredients together and set aside.
Rub the chicken with the oil, salt, pepper, cumin and garlic powder. Wash your hands after handling raw chicken.
Heat the grill or grill pan to medium-high. Cook the chicken 5 to 7 minutes per side, until a thermometer in the thickest part reads 165°F.
Rest 5 minutes on a clean plate, then slice and top with the salsa.
recipes.make_ahead: Make the salsa up to 1 day ahead.

freezer.text: Freeze cooked chicken up to 3 months; make salsa fresh.

leftovers.text: Slice cold chicken into a salad or wrap, or reheat to 165°F.

recipes.kids: Leave the jalapeño out of a small bowl of salsa for kids.

prep_day.ahead: Make the salsa; pound the chicken.

recipes.name: Grilled Peaches and Plums with Honey Yogurt
recipes.summary: Halved peaches, nectarines and plums grilled until caramelized, served with honey yogurt.
steps: Heat the grill or grill pan to medium. Rinse the fruit before cutting.
Brush the cut sides of the fruit with oil.
Grill cut side down 4 to 5 minutes, until marked and starting to soften, then turn and grill 2 minutes more.
Stir the yogurt with half the honey and the cinnamon. Serve the fruit warm with the yogurt and a drizzle of the rest of the honey.
recipes.make_ahead: Halve and pit the fruit up to 1 day ahead.

freezer.text: Do not freeze.

recipes.kids: Let the fruit cool a few minutes before giving it to kids; grilled fruit holds heat. Honey is not safe for babies under 1 year old.

swaps.dairy_free: Use a dairy-free yogurt.

recipes.name: Plum Kuchen
recipes.summary: A German-style plum cake: a soft butter cake topped with rows of plums and cinnamon sugar.

ingredients.prep: halved, pitted and cut in quarters

steps: Heat the oven to 350°F. Grease and flour the pan.
Beat the butter and sugar until fluffy. Beat in the eggs one at a time, then the vanilla.
Mix the flour, baking powder and salt. Add to the butter mixture in two parts, alternating with the milk, mixing just until smooth.
Spread the batter in the pan. Press the plum pieces into the top, skin side down, in tight rows.
Mix the sugar and cinnamon and sprinkle over. Bake 40 to 45 minutes, until a toothpick in the cake part comes out clean. Cool 20 minutes before cutting.
recipes.make_ahead: Keeps 2 days at room temperature, covered, or 4 days in the fridge.

freezer.text: Freeze squares wrapped well for up to 3 months.

recipes.kids: Kids can press the plums into the batter in rows.

swaps.dairy_free: Use dairy-free butter and a plant milk.

prep_day.ahead: Bake the cake.

recipes.name: Roasted Plums with Yogurt and Granola
recipes.summary: Plums roasted with honey and cinnamon until syrupy, spooned over yogurt with granola.
steps: Heat the oven to 400°F. Rinse the plums.
Set the plum halves cut side up in the dish. Drizzle with honey and orange juice and sprinkle with cinnamon.
Roast 15 to 20 minutes, until soft and juicy.
Spoon the yogurt into bowls, top with the warm or cold plums and their syrup, and finish with granola.
recipes.make_ahead: Roasted plums keep 5 days in the fridge.

freezer.text: Freeze roasted plums with their syrup up to 3 months.

recipes.kids: Honey is not safe for babies under 1 year old.

swaps.dairy_free: Use a dairy-free yogurt.

prep_day.ahead: Roast a pan of plums for the week.

recipes.name: Sheet-Pan Plum Ginger Chicken
recipes.summary: Chicken thighs roasted with plums, red onion, ginger and a soy-honey glaze. Sweet, savory and one pan.
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F. Stir the glaze ingredients together.
Toss the plums and onion with the oil on the baking sheet and push to the edges.
Season the chicken with salt and pepper, set it in the middle of the pan and brush with half the glaze. Wash your hands after handling raw chicken.
Roast 15 minutes. Brush the chicken with the rest of the glaze and stir the plums. Roast 10 to 15 minutes more, until a thermometer in the thickest thigh reads 165°F.
Rest 5 minutes, then serve with the plums and pan juices spooned over.
recipes.make_ahead: Mix the glaze and cut the onion up to 2 days ahead.

freezer.text: Freeze cooked chicken and plums up to 3 months. Reheat to 165°F.

leftovers.text: Slice over rice for lunch; reheat to 165°F.

recipes.kids: Serve a plain thigh and a few roasted plums for kids. Honey is not safe for babies under 1 year old.

swaps.gluten_free: Use tamari or a gluten-free soy sauce.

prep_day.ahead: Mix the glaze; cut the onion.

recipes.name: Cherry Almond Overnight Oats
recipes.summary: Oats, chia and milk soaked overnight with sweet cherries and almonds. Grab a jar and go.

ingredients.prep: pitted and halved, fresh or thawed frozen

steps: Stir the oats, chia, milk, yogurt, maple syrup and vanilla together.
Fold in 1 cup of the cherries. Divide among the jars and top with the rest of the cherries.
Cover and refrigerate at least 6 hours or overnight. Sprinkle with almonds before eating.
recipes.make_ahead: Keeps 4 days in the fridge.

freezer.text: The texture suffers when frozen.

recipes.kids: A grown-up pits the cherries; always check for pits before serving cherries to children.

swaps.dairy_free: Use a plant milk and dairy-free yogurt.
swaps.nut_free: Use pumpkin seeds instead of almonds.

prep_day.ahead: Fill jars for 4 days.

recipes.name: Chocolate Cherry Smoothie
recipes.summary: Frozen cherries, banana, cocoa and milk blended into a thick, not-too-sweet chocolate smoothie.
steps: Pour the milk into the blender and add the yogurt, banana, cherries, cocoa and vanilla.
Blend until smooth, about 1 minute. Serve right away.
recipes.make_ahead: Buy frozen pitted cherries, or pit and freeze fresh ones in summer.

freezer.text: Freeze pitted cherries up to 6 months.

recipes.kids: Kids can add the cocoa. Check that every cherry is pitted.

swaps.dairy_free: Use a plant milk and dairy-free yogurt.

recipes.name: Pork Tenderloin with Cherry Sauce
recipes.summary: Seared and roasted pork tenderloin with a quick pan sauce of sweet cherries, balsamic and thyme.

ingredients.prep: about 1 1/4 pounds each, silver skin trimmed
pitted and halved, fresh or frozen

steps: Heat the oven to 425°F. Pat the pork dry and season with salt and pepper. Wash your hands after handling raw pork.
Heat the oil in the skillet over medium-high heat. Brown the tenderloins on all sides, about 6 minutes.
Move the skillet to the oven and roast 12 to 15 minutes, until a thermometer in the thickest part reads 145°F. Move the pork to a cutting board and rest at least 3 minutes.

Set the skillet over medium heat (the handle is hot; use a mitt). Cook the shallot 1 minute. Add the cherries, vinegar, honey, broth and thyme and simmer 5 to 7 minutes, until the cherries soften and the sauce thickens.
Remove the thyme stems and stir in the butter. Slice the pork and spoon the sauce over.

safety.food: beef, pork or lamb steaks, chops and roasts

recipes.make_ahead: Pit the cherries up to 2 days ahead.

freezer.text: Freeze sliced cooked pork in the sauce for up to 3 months. Reheat to 165°F.

leftovers.text: Slice cold pork thin for sandwiches, or reheat to 165°F.

recipes.kids: Pork cooked to 145°F can be a little pink inside and is safe after the rest. Honey is not safe for babies under 1 year old.

swaps.dairy_free: Skip the butter.

prep_day.ahead: Trim the pork; pit the cherries.

recipes.name: Cherry Clafoutis
recipes.summary: A French country dessert: cherries baked in a puffy, custardy pancake batter. Simple and lovely warm.
steps: Heat the oven to 350°F. Butter the pie plate and spread the cherries in it.
Blend or whisk the eggs, milk, sugar, flour, vanilla and salt until smooth.
Pour the batter over the cherries.
Bake 35 to 40 minutes, until puffed, golden and set in the center (160°F).
Cool 15 minutes; it settles as it cools. Dust with powdered sugar if you like and cut into wedges.
recipes.make_ahead: Best the day it is baked. Keeps 2 days in the fridge.

freezer.text: The custard weeps when frozen.

recipes.kids: Kids can pour the batter. A grown-up pits the cherries.

swaps.dairy_free: Use a plant milk and oil for the dish.
